provenance.replaces: pearl/jade Calm Financial Clarity (frosted glass + Geist) — removed 2026-11-23
provenance.rolloutState: Shipped and finish-reviewed on every surface — proving surface /entries/new, the three dashboards, ledger, reports, settlements (list and detail), reconcile (overview and upload), months close, the admin family, login and /download. No rollout remains pending.
provenance.themeEngine: color-scheme: light on :root and color-scheme: dark on [data-theme='dark'] (src/app.css), so native control chrome follows the theme. [data-theme='dark'] .btn-stamp re-asserts solid jet red var(--accent) because dark .glass out-specifies .btn-stamp — the stamp stays solid at night, never outline. The dead --c-ink/--c-muted legacy tokens are fully swept from all components; only the documented token names (--ink, --muted, --surface, --pearl-border, --accent, --accent-2, --carbon, --radius) remain in use.

display.purpose: Page titles on navy coupon-head bands; Archivo 800.

label.purpose: Field labels and table heads — Archivo Narrow 700 uppercase, +0.08em.

micro-label.purpose: A deliberate ramp step at 10px (.tab-caps, Archivo Narrow 700, +0.08em uppercase), not a fallback — carries VOID/status chips, date-flag internals and serial previews, and holds AA at its sizes.

tab.purpose: Notched tab-caps and the stamp button — Archivo Narrow 700, +0.14em.

money.purpose: The only voice for money, serials and timestamps — Spline Sans Mono tabular.

shadows.name: paper-lift
shadows.purpose: The single sanctioned elevation: a contact line plus a wide low navy-tinted falloff under coupon-white stubs. Dark theme swaps to black equivalents.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button lift (-1px) on hover and press (+1px) on active. Fully collapsed under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.value: 768px — desktop navy rail appears; floating pill hides

components.name: Stamp Button (primary)

narrative.overview:
The month is a coupon wallet. Every payment is filed as a carbon stub — a notched tab-cap head carrying a serial, a red date flag riding the edge, a hairline fare-box split of the money, and a dashed tear-off perforation above the one red action that stamps the stub into the wallet. Nothing behind a filed stub changes: a voided entry is stamped VOID, a closed month carries the seal, corrections are new stubs that supersede old ones. The world refuses the category default of floating white cards on a grey SaaS ground; colour owns whole regions instead of accenting chips.

Carrier navy #0D1B3D is the shell: the desktop rail, the mobile pill, and every page's coupon-head band are navy regions set with the .on-navy scope, which re-points the ink tokens so ordinary markup reads correctly on the band. Jet red #D7262D is scarce by design — the primary action, the date flag, and alert accents and nothing else. Carbon purple #4B2E83 is the ink of money: every entered figure and every amount sets in tabular mono at carbon. Coupon white stubs are paper — solid, crisp, never blurred; the old frosted chrome is retired, and .glass is now a paper material with a quiet navy-tinted lift.

WCAG AA (>= 4.5:1 body, >= 3:1 large) in light and dark themes is a hard constraint, as are 44px minimum touch targets and the prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-reduced-transparency, and prefers-contrast: more media contracts. The dark theme is the same wallet at night: navy night ground, lifted band, carbon figures set in lavender.
keyCharacteristics: Colour owns regions (navy bands), not accent chips.
Money always sets in tabular mono at carbon; labels set in narrow caps.
Stubs are paper: solid fills, hairline borders, no backdrop blur anywhere.
One red primary per screen — the stamp action.
Dashed perforations separate the stub from its action zone.
Reserved devices held as headroom: security-dot guilloche, void-red hatch, carbon-copy lavender treatment, chamfered ticket corners, /// hatch marks.

rules.name: The Colour Owns Regions Rule
rules.body: Navy owns whole regions — bands, rails, pills — through the .on-navy scope, which re-points --ink, --muted, --surface and --pearl-border so children read navy-safe without markup changes. Colour is never applied as a chip-level accent to fake structure; red accents an action, navy declares a region.

rules.name: Approved status washes
rules.body: LedgerRow's internal amber/red/blue washes are approved status accents — they mark void, superseded and pending states inside a stub, not structure, so they do not break the Colour Owns Regions Rule.

rules.name: The Carbon Ink Rule
rules.body: Every entered figure, amount, serial and money value sets in Spline Sans Mono with tabular-nums (.carbon-nums), in carbon purple. Money never sets in the sans face and never in a colour other than carbon (dark: carbon night).

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Stubs are paper. Solid fills, one hairline border, no backdrop-filter, no translucency in primary surfaces; .glass-subtle translucency exists only as a background wash and collapses to solid under prefers-reduced-transparency and browsers without backdrop-filter support.

rules.name: The Two Ink Voices Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text is always Archivo Narrow 700 with tracking (labels, tabs, stamps); mono is always tabular and always for numbers. Sans never fakes either voice — no letter-spaced sans caps, no proportional digits in money.

dos: Do wrap any navy region in .on-navy so ink tokens flip automatically; never hand-pick light text colours per child.
Do set every amount, serial and numeric figure in .carbon-nums (tabular mono, carbon in light / carbon-night lavender in dark).
Do use .tab-caps (Archivo Narrow 700 uppercase, +0.08em) for field labels and table heads.
Do separate action zones from the stub with .perf perforations.
Do keep 44px touch targets, AA contrast in both themes, and the reduced-motion/transparency/contrast media contracts on every new surface.
Do keep the red primary to one action per screen; use stub buttons and semantic fills for everything else.
Do keep UI strings in the i18n message catalog (src/lib/i18n/messages.ts).
donts: Don't apply backdrop blur or translucency to primary surfaces — stubs are paper (.glass is now a solid material despite its name).
Don't use jet red as decoration, for selection states, or for more than the primary action, the date flag, and alert/void accents.
Don't re-import pearl/jade or frosted-glass values into the legacy token names (--pearl-*, .glass); the names are load-bearing for consumers, the old values are gone.
Don't reference Geist/Geist Mono (files remain in static/fonts/ unreferenced; new faces must come from the self-hosted world stack).
Don't invent serial digits or fixture amounts — serials preview as E-{CODE}-{YYYYMM}-······ until the server allocates, and paper-ledger fixtures are quoted exactly.
Don't convert entered figures to sans type or proportional digits; money's voice is fixed.
Don't rebuild the navy shell by hand-tinting each element — without .on-navy the token scope breaks for every child.
